problem: The F3 captured-tape hierarchy (ADR-0127 Decision.2) requires the parent data PUBLISH root to be CAPTURED by TWO distinct consumer documents: once by ReplayTapeManifestProducer (its inner data_captured_receipt) and once by ReplayRun (its separate replay-data CAPTURED receipt). The current F4 v1 WORM lifecycle (trust.py) and the P4 commit_p4_batch model both enforce exactly one CAPTURED per published stream: _require_head -> _p4_ledger._require_unclaimed refuses any stream already in a committed P4 batch, and _validate_capture_request cross-refuses legacy and P4 capture of the same stream.
evidence: trust.py:1820-1824 (_require_head -> _require_unclaimed), 2437-2441 (_validate_capture_request legacy/P4 cross-refusal), 5046-5049 (_require_unclaimed). Plan lines 527-530 (manifest-producer CAPTURED receipt) and 554-563 + 717-723 (ReplayRun replay-specific CAPTURED receipt on the same data entry).
decision_needed: How should a single PUBLISHED root be captured by multiple distinct consumer documents? Options: (A) authorize a bounded V2 multi-consumer capture extension to the P4/commit_p4_batch model (a published root may hold one CAPTURED receipt per distinct consumer port/document, while remaining one-time CONSUMED), as a separately-reviewed ADR/correction to ADR-0127 Decision.2; or (B) re-scope the composed-tape verification so the ReplayRun data entry reuses the manifest-producer's existing CAPTURED receipt rather than minting a second one (a design correction to the plan's two-receipt reading).
blocked_deliverable: compose_replay_tape (the 5-step composed-tape verification seam) and the three capture collaborators as runtime multi-consumer bindings. The CapturedReplayTape.v1 codec (slice 2a) is NOT blocked and proceeds independently.
